title: R Project
text:
Data
My data can be found in the palmerpenguins package
More details of the data can be found here: Data: Palmer Penguins, Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.
The data are released under the CC0 1.0 Universal public domain dedication, which waives all copyright and related rights, including the right to distribute. The dedication states that the data may be reused and redistributed “in any form whatsoever and for any purposes” (CC0 1.0 Universal).

title: R Project
text:
Process the Data
The data was first cleaned up so that it was useful for the analysis.

# Process the data
penguins_clean <- penguins |>
  drop_na(body_mass_g, bill_length_mm) |>          # remove the 2 penguins with missing measurements
  select(species, island, sex, body_mass_g, bill_length_mm) |>
  mutate(body_mass_kg = body_mass_g / 1000)        # add a column in kg

title: R Project
text:
Plot the Processed Data
From the processed data, can plot the individual events of the data to get a plot.

# Plot the processed data
bill_mass_plot <- ggplot(penguins_clean,
                         aes(x = body_mass_g, y = bill_length_mm, color = species)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Body Mass (g)",
    y = "Bill Length (mm)",
    color = "Species"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

bill_mass_plot







Figure 1: Bill length vs. body mass for Adelie, Chinstrap, and Gentoo penguins.

title: R Project
text:
Summary by Species
I grouped the penguins by species and calculated the sample size, mean body mass, and mean bill length for each.

# Summary by species
penguin_summary <- penguins_clean |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_mass_kg = mean(body_mass_kg),
    sd_mass_kg = sd(body_mass_kg),
    mean_bill_mm = mean(bill_length_mm),
    sd_bill_mm = sd(bill_length_mm),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_mass_kg))

# Display as a formatted table
knitr::kable(
  penguin_summary,
  col.names = c("Species", "n",
                "Mean mass (kg)", "SD mass (kg)",
                "Mean bill (mm)", "SD bill (mm)"),
  digits = c(0, 0, 2, 2, 1, 1),
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r")
)

from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

title: Python Project
text:
Data
The data come from the Palmer Station Antarctica LTER and were collected by Gorman et al. (2014). They are distributed in the palmerpenguins package, from which the CSV file used here was obtained.
The data are released under the CC0 1.0 Universal public domain dedication, which waives all copyright and related rights, including the right to distribute. The dedication states that the data may be reused and redistributed “in any form whatsoever and for any purposes” (CC0 1.0 Universal).

penguins = pd.read_csv("data/penguins.csv")

title: Python Project
text:
Processing the Data
Penguins with missing values in any of the four body measurements were removed before analysis.

measurements = {
    "bill_length_mm": "Bill Length (mm)",
    "bill_depth_mm": "Bill Depth (mm)",
    "flipper_length_mm": "Flipper Length (mm)",
    "body_mass_g": "Body Mass (g)",
}

penguins_clean = penguins.dropna(subset=list(measurements))

title: Python Project
text:
Summary by Species
The mean, standard deviation and sample size of each measurement were calculated for each species.

summary = (
    penguins_clean
    .groupby("species")[list(measurements)]
    .agg(["mean", "std", "count"])
)

# Build a readable table: one "mean ± sd" column per measurement
table = pd.DataFrame(index=summary.index)
table["n"] = summary[("body_mass_g", "count")]

for col, label in measurements.items():
    table[label] = (
        summary[(col, "mean")].round(1).astype(str)
        + " ± "
        + summary[(col, "std")].round(1).astype(str)
    )

table.index.name = "Species"
table

title: Python Project
text:
Visualizing the Summary
Figure 1 compares the mean of each measurement across species.

species = summary.index
colors = ["#F8766D", "#00BA38", "#619CFF"]   # ggplot2's default colours

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(10, 8))

for ax, (col, label) in zip(axes.flat, measurements.items()):
    means = summary[(col, "mean")]
    sds = summary[(col, "std")]
    bars = ax.bar(species, means, yerr=sds, capsize=5, color=colors, alpha=0.85)
    ax.bar_label(bars, fmt="%.1f", label_type="center", color="white")
    ax.set_title(label)
    ax.set_ylabel(label)
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)

fig.tight_layout()

fig_dir = Path("results/figures")
fig_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
fig.savefig(fig_dir / "penguin_measurements_by_species.png", dpi=300)
plt.show()







Figure 1: Mean penguin measurements by species. Error bars show ±1 standard deviation.
